text: of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version 4.5.12 MARINE BERTH As stated elsewhere in this report, one of the main reasons the proposed site was originally chosen for T- RICH was its access to existing Berth 30 in Port Tampa Bay. Technically, PTB has designated the shoreline immediately north of the site as Berth 29, indicating a potential future physical installation of a berth there. But there is no physical berth structure located there presently (though there could be in the event of a T-RICH expansion – see Section 3.9). Berth 30, which is just to the west of the proposed site but which the site has legal access to, is of relatively new design and in excellent condition. It is used infrequently to load and/or discharge 1) liquefied petroleum gas from the LPG operation on the site immediately to the east of T-RICH, and 2) bulk materials (e.g. cement) from the site immediately to the west. LPG is transferred between the plant and the berth via pipelines along the north edge of the T-RICH site. These pipelines are noted in Section 4.10 as being an obstacle to site construction that must be considered and protected during construction. Once T-RICH is in operation, these LPG pipelines should not be a concern as they are just outside the property boundary. Since Aptamus is already quite far along in the design of the CO ship intended to serve the T-RICH hub, it 2 was possible to lay the CO ship alongside the existing berth to evaluate its suitability to accommodate 2 the CO ship. There are several considerations, including: 2 1. The ship’s cargo loading manifold piping lines up with the CO loading arms on shore. 2 2. The flat side of the ship can make contact with at least 3 fenders near the fore, mid and aft ends of the ship. 3. Mooring bitts on shore or on dolphins are in suitable locations to receive the following 12 total mooring lines from the ship: a. Two bow lines b. Two breast lines forward c. Two breast lines aft d. Two spring lines forward e. Two spring lines aft f. Two stern lines When Aptamus’ CO ship design was laid alongside the existing berth in CAD, it was found that it was a 2 good match for the existing berth. The overall length of the berth is more than adequate for Aptamus’ ship. However, it was also determined that there is not enough room on the main dolphin, which houses the LPG hose tower and hose handling crane, to add the three required CO loading arms. The decision 2 was made to add an additional dolphin which will be dedicated to the CO loading arms. See Figure 4.24, 2 which depicts a bird’s eye view of the berth as it exists today. Figure 4.25 depicts the new CO Loading 2 Arm platform and CO pipeline. Figure 4.26 depicts the mooring line arrangement of the CO ship at Berth 2 2 30, ensuring that the ship can be securely moored during CO transfer operations. 2
